sources: SUNDAY Nov 1 2026 RUN, markets closed for a second day. Carries FRIDAY Oct 30 closes for VIX, Brent, DXY, gold, copper and the curve. ONE NEW DATAPOINT ON THE WHOLE BOARD and ONE CONFIRMED EVENT. HEADLINE: OPEC+ HELD DECEMBER TARGETS TODAY AS EXPECTED, SO THE ONE SCHEDULED WEEKEND RISK PASSED WITHOUT INCIDENT, AND THE SINGLE CLEANEST TEST OF FRIDAY SELLOFF - WHETHER HY CREDIT KEEPS WIDENING - IS STILL UNANSWERED BECAUSE FRED HAS NOT POSTED OCT 30. OPEC+ - DECEMBER TARGETS HELD. The seven core members (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan, Oman) agreed in principle online today to leave December output unchanged, per three Reuters sources. This matches what was expected at the Oct 31 run, so no surprise and no oil-negative shock into Monday. Note the reason given: most Gulf producers are pumping WELL BELOW their targets because the Iran war has disrupted exports, so a held target is not the same as held supply. The Q4 production-capacity review that sets 2027 baselines is still unfinished; roughly 2 mb/d of cuts remain to be unwound and the unwind path depends on that review. BREAKEVEN - THE ONLY TILE THAT MOVED. FRED T5YIFR posted OCT 30 at 2.22 pct, giving back 1bp from 2.23. Against 2.20 on Oct 23 it is still PLUS 2bp, so the tile stays UP for a third run, but the inflation-expectation impulse is fading at the margin rather than building. Tile 2.23 to 2.22. CREDIT - STILL THE OPEN QUESTION, SECOND RUN BLIND ON THE DECISIVE DAY. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 remains at 3.26 pct for OCT 29, page last updated Oct 30 09:21 CDT; the OCT 30 print - the day VIX jumped 12.9 pct - has NOT posted and will not before Monday. Tile carried at 326bp. Against 338bp a week ago the trend tile stays DOWN, but recall the direction flipped on Thursday (3.14 Oct tight, 3.18 Oct 27, 3.26 Oct 29). Treat the DOWN trend arrow as describing last week, not Friday. This is the first thing to re-read next run: if HY widened on Oct 30 alongside a 19.42 VIX, Friday was contagion; if it held near 326, Friday was a tech reset. CURVE - UNCHANGED AT THE HIGH. FRED T10Y2Y Oct 30 at 0.38, confirmed as final (updated Oct 30 16:03 CDT), a new high for the move. Against 0.31 on Oct 23 that is PLUS 7bp, tile UP for a third run. Ten-year 4.94 pct, down 4bp on Friday despite the equity rout - a small but real sign the rates market was not the driver on the day. VOL - CARRIED. VIX 19.42 on the Oct 30 close, plus 12.91 pct, intraday high 22.31, highest since April. Against 19.45 on Oct 23 the tile is FLAT on the week: a round trip to last Friday level, not a new vol regime. S&P 500 closed 7,580.07, minus 1.82 pct. Nasdaq minus 2.9 pct, worst day since June 5, and October closed minus about 5 pct, its worst month since March 2025. Driver was AI capex, not macro: Amazon on a record negative 42 bn USD twelve-month FCF, Alphabet still sliding after its earnings miss, Intel minus 26-29 pct on a weak Q4 outlook. Meta and Alphabet now more than 20 pct off 52-week highs, Tesla minus 19 pct, Amazon minus 15 pct, Nvidia minus 12 pct. OIL - CARRIED AT 113.43, AND READ THE ROLL NOTE BEFORE READING THE TILE. The December contract EXPIRED Friday at 117.64 USD; the JANUARY contract is now front month and settled at 113.43 USD, plus 2.37 pct on the day. The roll alone takes about 4 USD off the headline, so the tile LOOKS lower than the market is. Brent ROSE on Friday and is plus about 13.6 pct on the month from near 100-102 USD. WTI 104.12. Against 111.70 on Oct 23 the tile is UP. GULF - OCTOBER WAS THE WORST MONTH FOR SHIPPING SINCE THE WAR BEGAN, AND IT IS STILL ESCALATING. Vessels targeted across the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman and Arabian Gulf in October ran at more than TWICE September count, the highest since the start of the war. Friday first-known-successful limpet-mine strike (UKMTO) stands. Over the weekend: Saudi air defences intercepted a Houthi drone over RIYADH, a Houthi missile damaged Aden airport, Israel is reportedly updating a target list for possible new strikes on Iran, Rubio warned of an Iranian threat to Gulf states, and Iran Araghchi said red lines are a thing of the past. Pakistan military calls US-Iran mediation cautiously optimistic. STILL NO SAUDI CONFIRMATION of the Houthi claims on Ras Tanura, Rabigh and Abqaiq - FOURTEENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN unconfirmed. Note also a caution from the live feed: viral images of ship damage were FALSELY linked to an Iranian attack, so weekend social-media claims on Gulf infrastructure need confirmation before they move the board. METALS - COPPER-GOLD HOLDS 1.67 ON TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCE SETS. Gold fell hard again Friday, its third straight loss and its lowest close in at least twelve months, cited directly as Fed-hike positioning. Spot read 3,875.84 USD minus 3.62 pct with copper 6.4585 USD/Lbs gives 1.6663; the Friday-close read of gold Dec futures 3,898.90 with copper 6.51 USD/Lbs gives 1.6697. Both round to 1.67, up from 1.57 a week ago, trend UP. THE COMPOSITION WARNING STANDS AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE BOARD: copper FELL too. This is gold collapsing faster, i.e. the safety bid unwinding into a hawkish Fed and a 4.94 pct ten-year, NOT copper leading. A gold-driven copper-gold high is a much weaker pro-growth signal than a copper-driven one and must not be read as risk appetite on a week when equities fell. DOLLAR - FLAT FOR A THIRD RUN AND STILL A PUZZLE. DXY 101.88-101.92 on the Oct 30 close, minus about 0.12-0.15 pct, against 101.79-101.81 a week ago, so FLAT. Hot Q3 GDP at 3.4 pct, re-accelerating core PCE at 3.1 pct, two hike dissents, two more hawkish regional presidents (Musalem, Barkin) and a 4.94 pct ten-year have bought the dollar nothing in three sessions. Either the dollar is wrong or the December hike pricing is. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - CARRIED, STILL EASY. NFCI minus 0.487 for the week ending OCT 23 (minus 0.494 Oct 16, minus 0.501 Oct 9), updated Oct 28. Tile minus 0.49, FLAT. Next update WEDNESDAY NOV 4 and it will be the FIRST NFCI containing any of Friday vol. GLOBAL LIQUIDITY - STILL 1 (STABLE). FRED WALCL Oct 28 at 6,745,635 million USD, MINUS 7,969 million on the week (6,753,604 Oct 21, 6,755,639 Oct 14). A slightly faster drain than the prior week minus 2,035 million but far too small to be a regime change; no change at the ECB, PBOC or BOJ, which held at 1.25 pct. Tile 1. Next WALCL THURSDAY NOV 5. LABOUR - CARRIED, NO NEW PRINT. Initial claims 194k for the week ending OCT 24 (195k Oct 17, 200k Oct 10, 198k Oct 3), updated Oct 29. Against 195k a week ago the tile is FLAT. Next print THURSDAY NOV 5. No labour-market crack anywhere on the board. MACRO TILES - ALL CARRIED. ISM Manufacturing 54.5 September, NEXT PRINT TOMORROW MONDAY NOV 2 - the first hard macro test of the week. Consumer sentiment 48.0, UMich October final, a five-month low. Building permits 1,398k SAAR September revised. Sahm Rule 0.00 September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50. LEI y/y plus 1.2 pct carried and LOW PRECISION - the Oct 22 Conference Board release has the index unchanged at 99.6 and publishes no y/y figure. All FLAT. BLIND SPOTS - MOVE IS NOW SEVENTEEN RUNS STALE AND IT IS THE EXPENSIVE GAP. The MOVE index is CARRIED at 103.31 for OCT 23 for a SEVENTEENTH consecutive run: Investing.com historical table still ends at Oct 23 (106.84 Oct 22, 95.94 Oct 21, 101.70 Oct 20, 101.30 Oct 19, 101.10 Oct 16), and MacroMicro failed to serve again. TREAT THE MOVE TILE AS BLIND, NOT AS CALM - it is held FLAT by default across the exact window where equity vol jumped 13 pct, the ten-year sits at 4.94 pct and a December hike is being priced. Rate vol is the one reading that would separate an equity event from a rates event, and we cannot see it. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread is a STANDING ASSUMPTION at 0bp and the EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis a STANDING ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp, not measurements; every free source serves a SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread. FRED multi-series and CSV endpoints again refused to serve this run, so all FRED reads came from the series HTML pages. Scorecard unchanged: two assumed tiles, one judgement tile (global liquidity), one stale tile (MOVE), one low-precision carry (LEI) out of eighteen. CALENDAR - THE BUSIEST WEEK IN A MONTH: ISM Manufacturing MONDAY NOV 2. US MIDTERMS TUESDAY NOV 3, with a reported post-midterm US decision on resuming strikes on Iran. NFCI WEDNESDAY NOV 4. WALCL and jobless claims THURSDAY NOV 5. Sahm FRIDAY NOV 6. October CPI mid-November. Next FOMC December. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD 289bde8, the Oct 31 commit); this scheduled session remains the SOLE writer of data.json; the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17; BDTI stays removed since Oct 17. The .git lock-file pile keeps growing because this session cannot delete files in the folder - still harmless, but it WILL eventually break a git operation, and clearing it needs delete permission on the Dashboard Macro folder. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, SEVENTEENTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in PLAIN TEXT in .git/config; fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Untracked junk still in the repo root: _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: NOTHING BROKE OVER THE WEEKEND. The macro board is UNCHANGED AND STILL REFLATIONARY - growth hot, labour fine, conditions easy, credit inside last week, curve steepening at a new high, copper-gold at a new high but for the wrong reason - while the PRICE side has cracked in two specific places: the AI complex and the Gulf. Friday was not a macro repricing; it was a 13 pct VIX day driven by AI capex disappointments and a 4.94 pct ten-year, landing on a board where nothing recessionary is visible. OPEC+ removed one risk today. The three live threats into this week are an ISM miss MONDAY after a 3.4 pct GDP print, the MIDTERMS TUESDAY plus the reported post-midterm Iran decision, and a confirmed hit on Saudi crude infrastructure, which is closer than it was given October record attack count. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: whether HY posts wider than 326bp for Oct 30, which is the single cleanest test of whether Friday was contagion or a tech reset; ISM Monday; the midterms Tuesday; NFCI Wednesday as the first conditions read containing Friday; getting a live MOVE print; whether gold keeps collapsing or the safety bid returns; whether the dollar ever responds to hot US data; rotating the embedded PAT; clearing the .git lock files.
